title: Learn a rare accepted pure state from ordinary preparations
statement: Positive weight comparison controls conditioning under quantitative support and coupling promises.

evidence.quote: ## 5. Acquisition: learn the accepted state without collecting accepted copies

requires: B is a real symmetric entrywise nonnegative PAIR-AMPLITUDE matrix with ||B||_2<1, not an ordinary covariance matrix. The state is det(I-B^2)^(1/4) exp(a^daggerT B a^dagger/2)|0>. Partition B=(A,V;V^T,C), specify a complete Fock herald h with H=sum h_i, and retain collisions. Supplied-model computation uses rational B and the stated general perfect-matching FPRAS with worst-case bit complexity and logarithmic confidence dependence. Learning an unknown source additionally assumes known zero support, B_ij>=b_min>0 on that support, ||B||<=1-g with g>0, stationary independent preparations, and calibrated heterodyne measurements in the specified phase convention.
provides: Heterodyne alpha=x+iy gives Sigma=2E[xx^T]=(I-B)^-1 and B=I-Sigma^-1, with I/2<=Sigma<=I/g. Support-preserving stable inversion, clipping and a spectral check recover a rational physical model with entrywise error beta from O((m+log(1/delta_cal))/(g^2*beta^2)) unconditioned copies.

W_B(h,n)=haf(B_(h,n))^2/(h!n!) is a nonnegative homogeneous polynomial of degree H+N. For N<=L, entrywise error beta gives e^-alpha W_B<=W_Bhat<=e^alpha W_B, alpha=2(H+L)beta/b_min, before normalization. With mu_star=4(H+m/2)/g and L>=mu_star/t0, TV<=2t0+tanh(alpha), and the absolute log yield ratio is <=2m*beta/g+alpha-log(1-t0).

Take t0=eps/8, L=ceil(8mu_star/eps) and beta=min(g/(4m),b_min/2,eps*b_min/[8(H+L)],eps*g/(8m)). Conditional TV<=eps/2 and log relative yield error<=3eps/4 on calibration success. The sufficient sample count is O((m+log(1/delta_cal))*(H+m)^2/(g^4*b_min^2*eps^4)).

Finite coordinate range O(sqrt(g^-1 log(K_cal*m/delta_cal))) and resolution O(beta/[m(R+1)]) suffice. Known pure loss kappa in the CALIBRATION detector gives Sigma_obs=(1-kappa)I+kappa Sigma and a kappa^-2 sample factor; this does not cover loss in the herald experiment.

All promised Fock amplitudes are nonnegative, so the accepted pure state is sum_n sqrt(P_B(n|h))|n>. TV error eta implies half-trace error <=sqrt(2eta). A compact learned state description does not physically produce copies of a rare accepted state.
assumptions: This is source-reported model mathematics, with no new Capital proof review or replay. Positivity of covariance entries does not establish positivity of pair amplitudes. General complex phases, mixed retained states, unknown loss during heralding, arbitrary detector faults and hidden contamination are excluded. An upstream contamination weight much larger than the herald probability can dominate the accepted state; this is model-based prediction, not certification against arbitrary contamination. Relative fidelity F does not mean relative accuracy in 1-F. Physical resource production still pays 1/P_B(h). Vanishing unknown couplings require data. The external matching FPRAS was not re-proved, implemented or benchmarked by this source; demanding polynomial constants do not imply practical performance. The individual P2 prototype remains uncollected. The latent activated-Pauli decomposition does not finish general correlated decoding. No measured hardware advantage, universal quantum computer or full priority determination is supplied.
costs: Computation is polynomial in mode count, H, input bit length, inverse accuracy and the actual residual energy bound, not merely log energy. The sampler uses at most H^2 approximate matching counts on graphs with at most 2H ports, relative O(eps/H) error per call and a paid confidence allocation. Rational weight gadgets have polynomial bit overhead. With mu_C=tr[C^2(I-C^2)^-1], M=4(1+mu_C)(H+r/2) and L=ceil(4M/eps), the full visit tail is bounded. Calibration uses O((m+log(1/delta_cal))*(H+m)^2/(g^4*b_min^2*eps^4)) unconditioned preparations; known calibration-detector loss kappa adds kappa^-2. Dense covariance formation costs O(K_cal*m^2); finite resolution and random bits are paid. Pure-state half-trace error <=sqrt(2 TV) requires correspondingly tighter distribution accuracy. Faint unknown couplings give an Omega(theta^-2) preparation lower bound.
